items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: I was asking him about all the clarinet players... who was better, Jimmy Noon or Tio... I can't remember anything specific.

ctx.x: Did he mark fingering, or did he mark the rhythm or time or counting, or what did he mark?

He marked, uh, he checked certain lines for me to practice, and he told me how to, how to beat my foot. He says to beat 4-4, except if it's a fast tune, and then beat 2-4. Yeah. And, uh, uh, I was having a lot of lip trouble at the time, uh, very weak lip. I've always had some kind of trouble like that, but at that time, particularly bad. And he was telling me to play octaves, play a lot of octaves, which, uh, later on, I've come to appreciate, is pretty good advice for this. Slurdoms? Well, both, both, uh, he…
Uh, did he ever, uh, to get back to that one detail of counting, did he ever talk, insist on you stomping your foot all the time, or did he say anything about that much?
